mango-chicken.name: Aldi spicy mango marinated chicken (check label)

crispy-chicken.name: Ready-made crispy chicken breast fillets (check brand)

recipes.title: Mediterranean Beef & Couscous Bowls
recipes.subtitle: Lemony couscous, warmly spiced beef and all the fresh things.
steps: Fluff things up
Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl. Add boiling water using the packet’s couscous-to-water ratio, cover and stand for the packet time, then fluff with a fork. Stir through half the lemon juice.
Chop the crunch
Dice the cucumbers and halve the tomatoes. Crush the garlic. Mix the yoghurt with the remaining lemon juice and half the garlic. Keep chilled until serving.
Bring on the beef

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mince for 8–10 minutes, breaking it up. Stir in cumin, oregano, remaining garlic, salt and pepper for the last 2 minutes. Check the mince reaches 75°C in the centre.
Build your own bowl
Divide the couscous, beef and salad between bowls. Crumble over feta and add the lemon yoghurt. Let everyone keep their favourite bits separate if they like.
recipes.family: Serve the salad and yoghurt in little bowls so everyone can build their own. For milder plates, put a little cooked beef aside before adding spices.
recipes.kidJob: Crumble the feta and fluff the cooled couscous with a fork, with an adult nearby.

nutrition.note: Fresh vegetables add crunch and fibre; lean beef contributes iron. Wholemeal couscous is an easy fibre swap.

recipes.allergens: Wheat/gluten and milk. Check couscous, yoghurt and spice packaging.
recipes.variation: Use cooked lentils instead of beef for a meat-free version; amounts and nutrition will change.
recipes.prepTip: Chop the salad and mix the yoghurt earlier in the day; refrigerate separately.

recipes.title: Japanese Pork Tonkatsu with Crunchy Slaw & Sweet Potato Wedges
recipes.subtitle: Golden panko pork, rainbow slaw and sweet potato wedges.
steps: Wedges first

Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Cut the sweet potato into even wedges, toss with one-third of the oil and a pinch of the measured salt. Spread over a lined tray and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning halfway, until tender.
Make it crunchy
Finely shred the cabbage and grate the carrots. Toss with yoghurt and vinegar; refrigerate. Stir the barbecue, soy and Worcestershire sauces together in a separate serving bowl.
Crumb the pork

Pat the pork dry and flatten to an even 1 cm thickness. Put flour, beaten egg and panko in three shallow bowls. Season the flour with remaining salt and pepper. Coat pork in flour, then egg, then crumbs. Discard unused coating that touched raw pork.
Golden hour

Heat remaining oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the pork for about 4–5 minutes per side, in batches, until golden and cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C. Lower the heat if the crumb browns too fast. Rest 3 minutes, slice and serve with slaw, wedges and sauce on the side.
recipes.family: Keep the sauce separate for little dippers. Serve raw carrot sticks instead of dressed slaw for anyone who prefers it.
recipes.kidJob: Mix the slaw dressing and set out little sauce bowls. An adult handles raw pork and the hot pan.

nutrition.note: Sweet potato and cabbage bring colour and fibre. A shallow fry keeps the crumb crisp; actual absorbed oil varies.

recipes.allergens: Wheat/gluten, egg, milk, soy and possibly fish in Worcestershire sauce. Check all sauce labels.
recipes.variation: Chicken breast works too: flatten evenly and check it reaches 75°C. Use fish-free Worcestershire if needed; check the label.
recipes.prepTip: Cut the wedges and shred the slaw first. Keep raw meat and salad utensils separate.

recipes.title: Loaded Beef Burrito Bowls
recipes.subtitle: Smoky beef, rice, black beans and a choose-your-own topping party.
steps: Rice on, music on
Cook the rice following packet directions. Brown rice may take longer; start it first. Drain and rinse the black beans and corn.
Get the toppings ready
Shred the lettuce, halve the tomatoes, dice the avocado and cut the lime into wedges. Dice the onion and crush the garlic.
Make the smoky middle

Heat the oil in a large pan. Soften the onion for 4 minutes. Add mince, breaking it up for 8–10 minutes, then garlic, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper. Stir for 1 minute. Add beans, corn and a splash of water. Simmer until hot throughout and the mince reaches 75°C.
Load ’em up
Spoon rice and beef into bowls. Add lettuce, tomatoes, avocado, cheddar, yoghurt and salsa. Finish with a squeeze of lime. Keep salsa mild and let grown-ups add their own heat.
recipes.family: A toppings bar is the whole point. Keep a few beans and some corn separate before they go into the beef.
recipes.kidJob: Wash and tear the lettuce, then arrange the topping bowls.

nutrition.note: Black beans add fibre and plant protein. Adjust rice and toppings to appetite rather than expecting identical portions.

recipes.allergens: Milk. Check salsa and spice labels for additional allergens.
recipes.variation: For a lighter appetite, use a smaller rice portion and more lettuce. For meat-free bowls, replace beef with extra beans; quantities will differ.
recipes.prepTip: Cook the beef-and-bean mixture ahead and refrigerate promptly. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.title: Fresh Italian Chicken, Zucchini & Tomato Pasta
recipes.subtitle: Juicy tomatoes, golden chicken, basil and lemon. No cream required.
steps: Get the pasta going
Bring a large pot of water to the boil and cook pasta following packet directions. Before draining, save a mug of the cooking water.
Prep the fresh bits
Slice the zucchini into half-moons, halve the tomatoes and crush the garlic. Zest and juice the lemon. Cut chicken into even bite-sized pieces using a separate board.
Golden chicken, juicy tomatoes

Heat half the oil in a large pan. Cook chicken for 7–10 minutes, turning, until its centre reaches 75°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Add remaining oil, zucchini and tomatoes to the pan and cook 5–6 minutes. Stir in garlic and oregano for 1 minute.
Toss it all together

Return chicken to the pan with pasta and spinach. Add lemon zest, half the juice, salt, pepper and a splash of pasta water. Toss until spinach wilts and everything is hot. Add torn basil and parmesan. Taste before adding more lemon juice.
recipes.family: Keep some plain pasta aside before tossing. Finely grate zucchini into the sauce for anyone who prefers smaller veggie pieces.
recipes.kidJob: Tear the basil leaves and sprinkle the parmesan at the table.

nutrition.note: Chicken provides protein and the tomato-zucchini mix adds vegetables. Wholemeal pasta can increase fibre.

recipes.allergens: Wheat/gluten and milk; some pasta contains egg. Check the packet.
recipes.variation: Use gluten-free pasta or skip parmesan if needed, checking every product label. These swaps alter nutrition.
recipes.prepTip: Slice vegetables ahead. Keep raw chicken covered on the lowest fridge shelf.

recipes.title: Sweet Chilli & Soy Salmon/Chicken Bowls
recipes.subtitle: Sticky glaze, fluffy rice and bright greens. Salmon, chicken, or a bit of both.
steps: Start with the rice
Cook rice following packet directions. Cut broccoli into small florets, make carrot ribbons with a peeler and slice the cucumber. Finely grate ginger and crush garlic.
Stir up the sticky sauce

Mix sweet chilli sauce, soy, ginger, garlic and half the lime juice. Reserve half in a clean bowl for serving BEFORE anything touches raw meat or fish. Discard any sauce left after contact with raw protein.
Choose your Friday

Salmon: brush with a little oil and the cooking half of the glaze, then bake at 200°C fan-forced for around 12–15 minutes, depending on thickness, until opaque and flaking easily; check for bones. Chicken: cut into even strips and pan-fry in the oil for 7–10 minutes, turning, until the centre reaches 75°C; add the cooking glaze in the final 2 minutes. Mixed: divide oil and cooking glaze between the proteins, cook separately and use separate utensils.
Make it a bowl night

Steam broccoli for 4–5 minutes until just tender. Divide rice, protein, broccoli, carrot and cucumber into bowls. Add the reserved clean sauce and remaining lime to taste. For mixed plates, give each person their chosen protein.
recipes.family: Pick salmon, chicken or half-and-half above. For less heat, keep a portion of protein unglazed and offer sauce at the table.
recipes.kidJob: Arrange cucumber and carrot ribbons in the bowls. An adult handles the peeler and checks fish for bones.

nutrition.note: Salmon supplies omega-3 fats. Chicken is a leaner alternative. The vegetable mix adds colour, texture and fibre.

recipes.allergens: Soy and usually wheat/gluten in soy sauce; fish when salmon is selected. Check sweet chilli and soy labels. Mixed preparation is not suitable for avoiding fish cross-contact.
recipes.variation: Use reduced-salt tamari if avoiding wheat, checking it is labelled gluten-free. Sauce quantities are deliberately moderate; add to taste.
recipes.prepTip: Make the glaze ahead and refrigerate. Keep the serving half separate from raw protein.

recipes.title: Creamy Honey-Mustard Chicken with Mash & Greens
recipes.shortTitle: Creamy Honey-Mustard Chicken with Mash & Greens
recipes.subtitle: Golden chicken breast in a mild mustard sauce with buttery mash and greens.
steps: Prepare mash
Peel and chop potatoes. Boil in salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with butter and warmed milk.
Cook the chicken
Cut chicken breasts into even thin fillets; season lightly. Brown in oil over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side, then cook to 75°C in the centre. Set aside.
Make the sauce
In the same pan, soften crushed garlic for 30 seconds. Add stock, Dijon, wholegrain mustard and honey. Simmer 2–3 minutes and return chicken to coat. Thin with water if needed.
Serve the greens
Steam broccoli and beans for 4–5 minutes until bright and tender. Serve with mash and chicken, spooning over the sauce.
recipes.family: Offer sauce on the side for anyone who prefers their chicken plain.
recipes.kidJob: Help wash and portion the vegetables with adult supervision.
recipes.allergens: Milk and mustard; check stock ingredients.
recipes.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Chop potatoes and wash beans ahead; keep everything refrigerated.

nutrition.note: High-protein chicken breast with comforting mash and greens.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Salmon & Chicken Rice Bowls
recipes.subtitle: Sweet soy-glazed salmon for some and chicken breast for the kids, with rice and crunchy vegetables.
steps: Rice and vegetables
Cook rice using packet instructions. Thinly slice cucumber and carrot, cut avocado and steam broccoli.
Mix teriyaki
Mix soy, honey, vinegar, grated ginger, crushed garlic, sesame oil and 3 tablespoons of water. Set the sauce aside in a clean bowl.
Cook separately
Pan-cook salmon until opaque and cooked to preference. Fry sliced chicken separately to 75°C, keeping utensils separate to avoid fish cross-contact.
Glaze and assemble
Simmer the sauce in a clean pan; thicken with cornflour mixed with a splash of cold water. Coat salmon and chicken separately. Serve over rice with fresh vegetables and broccoli.
recipes.family: Cook chicken breast instead of salmon for Phoebe and Tobias; give everyone the same teriyaki glaze.
recipes.kidJob: Wash cucumber, portion rice and arrange vegetables.
recipes.allergens: Soy, fish, and possible wheat in soy sauce. Use separate utensils for fish and chicken.
recipes.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Mix sauce and cut vegetables ahead.

nutrition.note: Protein and calories depend on the chosen salmon/chicken mix.

recipes.title: Creamy Beef & Mushroom Stroganoff with Egg Noodles
recipes.shortTitle: Creamy Beef & Mushroom Stroganoff with Egg Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Tender beef strips and mushrooms in a quick creamy sauce with egg noodles.
steps: Cook the noodles
Cook egg noodles in boiling water according to packet instructions; reserve some cooking water.
Sear the beef
Pat strips dry. Sear in batches in a hot oiled pan 1–2 minutes per side, then remove to keep tender.
Make mushroom sauce
Cook sliced mushrooms and onion in butter for 5–6 minutes. Add crushed garlic, paprika and mustard for 30 seconds. Add stock and Worcestershire; simmer 3–4 minutes.
Finish gently
Reduce heat, stir in sour cream and return beef to warm through. Do not boil the cream sauce. Adjust with reserved noodle water and toss with noodles.
recipes.family: Serve mushrooms separately for fussy eaters.
recipes.kidJob: Help wash and portion the vegetables with adult supervision.
recipes.allergens: Milk, egg, wheat/gluten, mustard, possible fish in Worcestershire.
recipes.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Slice beef and mushrooms before school pick-up.

nutrition.note: Lean beef provides iron and protein; serve with extra greens if desired.

recipes.title: BBQ Pork & Pineapple Wraps with Crunchy Slaw
recipes.shortTitle: BBQ Pork & Pineapple Wraps with Crunchy Slaw
recipes.subtitle: Fast BBQ pork, juicy pineapple and fresh crunchy slaw in soft wraps.
steps: Prepare the crunch
Toss slaw mix with sliced cucumber. Stir yoghurt with vinegar and a little honey; dress at the last minute.
Sear the pork
Slice pork into thin strips, season with paprika and crushed garlic. Stir-fry in hot oil for 4–6 minutes until browned and thoroughly cooked.
Make it sticky
Add drained pineapple pieces to the pan for a minute. Stir in barbecue sauce and remaining honey, coating the pork.
Fill the wraps
Warm soft wraps. Divide pork and pineapple between wraps, add crunchy slaw and serve any extra sauce on the side.
recipes.family: Put pineapple, pork and slaw in separate bowls for everyone to choose.
recipes.kidJob: Help wash and portion the vegetables with adult supervision.
recipes.allergens: Wheat/gluten and milk. Check barbecue sauce and wrap labels.
recipes.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Make the yoghurt dressing and slice pork ahead.

nutrition.note: Amounts assume two soft wraps per serving.

recipes.title: Chicken & Egg Fried Rice
recipes.subtitle: Golden chicken, soft egg, peas and carrots in tasty soy-oyster fried rice.
steps: Get the rice ready
Cook rice ahead and chill promptly in a shallow container; keep refrigerated until cooking. Do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Cook chicken and eggs
Dice chicken and stir-fry until golden and 75°C internally. Remove. Scramble beaten eggs in the pan and set aside.
Fry vegetables and rice
Cook diced carrots for 3 minutes in oil, then add peas, garlic and grated ginger. Add cold cooked rice and stir-fry until thoroughly hot.
Finish and serve
Stir through soy, oyster sauce, vinegar and sesame oil. Return chicken and egg, toss until steaming hot and top with spring onion.
recipes.family: Serve toppings and sauce separately so the kids can build their own plates.
recipes.kidJob: Whisk eggs and wash spring onions.
recipes.allergens: Egg, soy, wheat/gluten in sauces and molluscs in oyster sauce.
recipes.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Cool rice quickly and refrigerate; reheat until steaming hot.

nutrition.note: Rice quantity is dry weight before cooking.

recipes.title: Family Beef Cheeseburgers with Salad
recipes.subtitle: Juicy beef patties with melted cheese, lettuce, tomato and pickles.
steps: Shape the patties
Divide beef mince into five patties slightly larger than burger buns. Season the outside just before cooking.
Cook burgers
Sear in a pan or barbecue over medium-high heat for about 4–5 minutes a side, until cooked through to 75°C internally. Add cheese for the last minute.
Prepare toppings
Wash and slice lettuce, tomatoes, onion and pickles. Toast buns briefly and stir tomato sauce with a little Dijon.
Let everyone build
Put buns, patties, cheese, salad and sauce on the table so everyone builds their own burger. Serve with fresh salad or optional chips.
recipes.family: Serve toppings and sauce separately so the kids can build their own plates.
recipes.kidJob: Set out the burger toppings.
recipes.allergens: Wheat/gluten, milk, mustard; check bun and sauce labels.
recipes.variation: Adjust carbohydrates and vegetables to each person's appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Shape patties ahead and refrigerate covered.

nutrition.note: Estimates exclude optional chips and extra toppings.

recipes.title: Thai Basil Beef & Vegetable Stir-Fry
recipes.subtitle: Savoury beef, colourful vegetables and a crispy egg, with just a little rice.
steps: Rice first
Get the rice cooking following the pack. Slice capsicum and carrots into thin strips; trim the beans. Mix soy, oyster sauce and honey in a mug.
Cook the beef
Heat half the oil in a big frying pan or wok. Brown mince over medium-high heat for 7–8 minutes, breaking it into small pieces; cook thoroughly to 75°C.
Add plenty of veg
Add capsicum, beans, carrots, ginger and a little garlic. Stir-fry for 4–5 minutes so the veg still has some bite. Toss with the sauce and basil; keep chilli on the table for adults.
Top with an egg
Fry five eggs in a separate pan until the whites are set. Spoon a modest amount of rice onto plates, heap over beef and vegetables, and add an egg.
recipes.family: Keep the stir-fry mild and add sliced chilli or hot sauce at the table. Kids can have egg cooked through.
recipes.kidJob: Trim beans and wash basil.
recipes.allergens: Soy, oyster/molluscs, wheat if conventional soy sauce is used, egg.
recipes.variation: Adjust vegetables and starch to appetite. Cook extra lean meat for a higher-protein adult portion.
recipes.prepTip: Use pre-cut stir-fry vegetables to keep prep under 10 minutes.

nutrition.note: Lean beef and egg are substantial protein sources; vegetables add fibre. Rice portion is moderate.

recipes.title: Crispy-Skin Salmon with Ginger & Sweet Chilli Slaw
recipes.shortTitle: Crispy-Skin Salmon with Ginger & Sweet Chilli Slaw
recipes.subtitle: Crackly skin, punchy ginger sauce and lots of crunchy slaw. Chicken alternative included.
steps: Make the crunchy salad
Use bagged slaw plus finely sliced red cabbage, cucumber and carrots. Toss with 1 tablespoon rice vinegar and a drizzle of sesame oil. Keep chilled.
Whisk the sauce
In a small saucepan gently warm sweet chilli, soy, grated ginger, remaining vinegar and two tablespoons water for 2 minutes. This is a sauce to drizzle alongside, not over the skin.
Make the skin properly crispy

Pat skin-on salmon thoroughly dry and lightly season it. Heat a non-stick frying pan with oil on medium-high. Cook skin-side down for 5–7 minutes, pressing gently for the first 20 seconds, until deep golden and crisp; turn and cook another 1–3 minutes until done to preference. Don't crowd the pan.
Cook chicken if chosen
For chicken eaters, slice chicken breast into thin even portions. Pan-cook in a separate clean skillet until 75°C inside. Serve with the same sauce, avoiding fish cross-contact.
Plate without soggy skin
Put slaw and avocado on plates, add fish skin-side up (or chicken), and spoon the ginger sauce around the side.
recipes.family: Chicken breast for Phoebe and Tobias; leave the salmon skin untouched by sauce so it stays crunchy.
recipes.kidJob: Mix slaw and arrange avocado.
recipes.allergens: Fish (salmon), soy, sesame, wheat if present in soy sauce. Check sweet chilli sauce.
recipes.variation: Add a small microwaved potato if someone needs extra carbohydrates; no rice required.
recipes.prepTip: Buy pre-shredded slaw to skip most of the cutting; keep salmon skin dry until frying.

nutrition.note: Salmon contributes omega-3 fats; protein depends on individual fish/chicken servings.

recipes.title: Aldi Spicy Mango Chicken Wraps
recipes.subtitle: Ready-marinated chicken, warm wraps and crisp fresh salad. The easiest night of the week.
steps: Check the chicken pack

Buy Aldi spicy mango marinated chicken in the meat section if stocked. Check the label for allergens, cook-by date and recommended method; substitute chicken breast with a suitable bottled mango marinade if unavailable.
Cook it through
BBQ, air-fry or pan-cook the marinated chicken following the pack's directions; ensure poultry reaches at least 75°C in the centre. Allow a brief rest, then slice.
Prep simple fillings
While the chicken cooks, wash and shred lettuce, slice cucumber and tomato, and cut avocado. Spoon yoghurt into a small bowl as a cooling option.
Wrap it up
Warm wraps briefly and set the chicken and salad in bowls. Let everyone make their own wrap; use yoghurt if the marinade is spicy.
recipes.family: The marinade may be too spicy for the kids: reserve plain chicken breast or offer extra yoghurt if needed.
recipes.kidJob: Lay out wraps and add the salad.
recipes.allergens: Check Aldi product and wraps: likely wheat/gluten; may contain milk, soy or other allergens. Yoghurt contains milk.
recipes.variation: Use lettuce cups instead of a wrap if preferred.
recipes.prepTip: Ready-marinated chicken, bagged lettuce and sliced veg keep prep at 5–10 minutes.

nutrition.note: Estimated assuming roughly 230 g raw marinated chicken and two wraps each; check Aldi packaging for accurate nutrition.

recipes.title: Crispy Chicken Burgers with Rainbow Slaw
recipes.shortTitle: Crispy Chicken Burgers with Rainbow Slaw
recipes.subtitle: Crispy breast fillets, a pile of crunchy slaw and a fresh burger bun.
steps: Get the chicken cooking
Preheat the air fryer or oven. Cook the ready-made crispy chicken breast fillets exactly as directed on the pack, until hot through and poultry reaches at least 75°C; time varies by brand.
Make quick rainbow slaw
Mix pre-shredded slaw, thin red cabbage, grated carrot and grated apple with yoghurt. Add burger sauce to taste, or serve separately.
Warm buns
Split and toast the burger buns lightly. Wash lettuce leaves and set out cheese slices.
Build burgers
Load buns with crispy chicken, cheese, lettuce and rainbow slaw. Offer extra slaw and carrot sticks on the side.
recipes.family: Leave slaw and sauce separate if Tobias prefers a simple chicken-and-cheese burger.
recipes.kidJob: Grate the apple with help and assemble buns.
recipes.allergens: Wheat/gluten, milk, egg and possible soy depending on bought chicken and sauce. Check packs.
recipes.variation: Add a second small chicken fillet for a higher-protein adult meal if needed.
recipes.prepTip: Use pre-cut coleslaw vegetables to make this a 10-minute prep dinner.

nutrition.note: Protein varies substantially by store-bought fillet size/brand. For a training-sized serving, aim for a chicken fillet with roughly 150–200 g chicken or add extra lean chicken.

recipes.title: Proper Aussie Family BBQ
recipes.subtitle: Steak, beef snags, BBQ onions, grilled corn and a proper big garden salad.
steps: Heat the barbie
Preheat the barbecue. Slice onions, halve the corn if preferred and prepare a big bowl of washed lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, avocado and beetroot.
Grill onions and corn
Start onions on the hotplate with a little oil and cook until sweet and golden. Grill corn, turning regularly, for about 10–12 minutes.
Cook the meats
Barbecue sausages until cooked through, following pack guidance and checking that minced sausage meat reaches 75°C. Cook steaks to preferred doneness, rest briefly and slice across the grain.
Put it on the table
Dress salad with a splash of vinegar and olive oil. Serve steak, a sausage if wanted, onions, corn and lots of garden salad for everyone to help themselves.
recipes.family: The meat and salads are on shared platters; kids can choose steak, sausage or both.
recipes.kidJob: Set out salad toppings and help prepare corn.
recipes.allergens: Check sausage ingredients for wheat/gluten, soy, sulphites and other allergens.
recipes.variation: Add microwaved baby potatoes if needed, but the BBQ stands on its own.
recipes.prepTip: Use pre-washed salad leaves, ready-cut corn and a bag of sliced beetroot.

nutrition.note: Varies with steak cut and sausage size. A steak-forward adult plate gives more protein with less processed meat.

recipes.title: Orange Chicken & Crunchy Vegetable Stir-Fry
recipes.subtitle: Tangy orange chicken breast, broccoli, snow peas and capsicum, with a little noodle.
steps: Mix the orange sauce
Whisk orange juice, zest of one orange, soy, honey, rice vinegar, ginger and half the cornflour. Set aside. Slice chicken breast into bite-sized pieces.
Brown the chicken
Toss chicken with remaining cornflour. Stir-fry in oil over medium-high heat in two batches for 6–8 minutes total or until fully cooked to 75°C. Remove and keep warm.
Crunch the veg
Add sliced capsicum, carrots, broccoli and snow peas to the pan with a splash of water. Stir-fry for 4–5 minutes, keeping the vegetables colourful and slightly crisp.
Glossy finish
Add the sauce and stir until bubbling and lightly thickened. Return chicken. Warm Hokkien noodles as directed on their pack, then toss with the chicken and vegetables; finish with spring onions.
recipes.family: Sauce is zesty, not spicy. Keep a little plain chicken and noodles aside before saucing for fussy eaters.
recipes.kidJob: Top plates with sliced spring onions.
recipes.allergens: Soy and possibly wheat/gluten in noodles and soy sauce; check labels.
recipes.variation: Adjust vegetables and starch to appetite. Cook extra lean meat for a higher-protein adult portion.
recipes.prepTip: Use a pre-cut stir-fry vegetable pack and ready-to-wok noodles for a faster night.

nutrition.note: Chicken breast delivers substantial protein; keep noodles moderate and vegetables generous.

recipes.title: TM5 Chicken, Mushroom & Spinach Risotto
recipes.subtitle: Creamy Parmesan risotto from the Thermomix with tender pan-cooked chicken and green vegetables.
steps: TM5: grate the Parmesan
Put the Parmesan in pieces into the clean, dry TM5 bowl. Grate 8 sec / speed 9. Tip into a bowl and set aside.
TM5: chop and soften
Put quartered onion and garlic in the bowl. Chop 5 sec / speed 5; scrape down. Add 15 ml oil and the sliced mushrooms. Sauté 4 min / 100°C / reverse / speed spoon.
TM5: start the risotto

Add arborio rice and cook 2 min / 100°C / reverse / speed spoon. Pour in 750 ml hot chicken stock, then cook 16 min / 100°C / reverse / speed spoon, with the simmering basket resting on the lid instead of the measuring cup. Check the 2.2 L bowl limit before cooking and stop if the mixture rises too high.
Cook chicken separately while the TM5 works

Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. In a large frying pan with remaining oil, cook in batches until golden and 75°C in the centre. This keeps the TM5 below its safe fill limit and gives the family a proper protein portion.
TM5: finish and stand

At the end of the cooking time check the rice; add a splash of hot stock and cook another 2–4 min / 100°C / reverse / speed spoon if still firm. Stir in thawed peas, spinach, butter and Parmesan using the spatula, close lid and stand 3–4 minutes until spinach is wilted and peas hot. Fold in cooked chicken in a serving bowl; do not force the full five-person batch back into the TM5.
recipes.family: A pan of chicken cooks alongside the TM5 risotto, avoiding a crowded bowl. Portion some risotto before adding mushrooms for anyone who dislikes them.
recipes.kidJob: Weigh the rice and wash spinach.
recipes.allergens: Milk; check stock for gluten, celery or other allergens.
recipes.variation: Adjust the vegetable and carbohydrate portions to appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Buy pre-sliced mushrooms; chicken can be chopped earlier and chilled.

nutrition.note: Pan-cooked 200 g raw chicken per serving supplies substantial lean protein. TM5 mixing bowl holds a maximum 2.2 L.

recipes.title: TM5 Beef & Bean Loaded Sweet Potatoes
recipes.shortTitle: TM5 Beef & Bean Loaded Sweet Potatoes
recipes.subtitle: Mild tomato-rich beef chilli, beans and corn over hot sweet potatoes with avocado and cheese.
steps: Start the sweet potatoes

Prick the sweet potatoes; microwave in batches 7–10 minutes until nearly soft (time depends on size), then finish in the air fryer at 200°C for about 10 minutes. For large potatoes, halve lengthways before cooking.
TM5: make the vegetable sauce

Place quartered onion and garlic into TM5 bowl; chop 5 sec / speed 5. Add oil and cook 3 min / 100°C / speed 1. Add chopped capsicum and chop 3 sec / speed 4. Add diced tomatoes, cumin, paprika and a little mild chilli powder. Simmer 12 min / 100°C / reverse / speed spoon, with simmering basket on the lid to allow steam to escape. Keep the bowl well below the 2.2 L maximum.
Brown beef in a pan
While the TM5 sauce cooks, brown the mince in a large frying pan over medium-high heat, breaking into small pieces; cook to at least 75°C throughout. Use a large pan to avoid crowding.
Finish the chilli in the pan

Tip TM5 tomato mixture into the beef pan. Drain and rinse black beans and corn; add to the pan and simmer about 6–8 minutes until piping hot. Add water if needed. The full beef-and-bean batch must not be packed into the TM5 bowl.
Serve loaded sweet potatoes
Split sweet potatoes, spoon over beef chilli, add grated cheddar, diced avocado and a little yoghurt. Put the toppings on the table for the family to help themselves.
recipes.family: Keep chilli powder minimal and offer extra hot sauce separately. The kids can choose beans and corn.
recipes.kidJob: Drain and rinse canned beans with help.
recipes.allergens: Milk; check spice blends and canned ingredients.
recipes.variation: Adjust the vegetable and carbohydrate portions to appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Pre-washed sweet potatoes and frozen chopped capsicum reduce prep.

nutrition.note: High-protein beef and beans, plenty of fibre and sweet potato. TM5 prepares the tomato sauce while beef cooks separately.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Salmon with Tomato & Herb Salsa
recipes.shortTitle: Mediterranean Salmon with Tomato & Herb Salsa
recipes.subtitle: Crispy-skinned salmon or chicken with balsamic tomato salsa, golden baby potatoes and green beans.
steps: Start the potatoes
Halve baby potatoes, toss with some olive oil and salt. Air-fry at 200°C for 18–23 minutes, shaking once, until golden and tender. Start these before preparing the rest.
Make the fresh salsa
Halve cherry tomatoes and finely tear basil. Toss with balsamic, a little oil, salt and pepper. Set aside while the proteins cook; keep it fresh rather than making a heavy sauce.
Cook fish or chicken separately

For salmon, pat skin completely dry. Pan-sear skin-side down in hot oil for 5–7 minutes until crisp; turn carefully and finish 1–3 minutes until cooked to preference. For chicken, pan-cook thin breast fillets in a separate pan until 75°C at the centre.
Steam the beans and plate
Steam trimmed green beans for 4–5 minutes until just tender. Serve salmon skin-up (or chicken) alongside potatoes and beans, with tomato salsa spooned next to the skin to keep it crisp.
recipes.family: Phoebe and Tobias have chicken breast with the same salsa and vegetables.
recipes.kidJob: Wash vegetables and help set out the serving bowls.
recipes.allergens: Fish if salmon selected; check any bottled balsamic ingredients.
recipes.variation: Adjust the vegetable and carbohydrate portions to appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Use pre-washed potatoes and pre-trimmed green beans.

nutrition.note: Values vary by salmon/chicken option. Crispy salmon skin is best left clear of the salsa.

recipes.title: Loaded Chicken & Vegetable Nachos
recipes.subtitle: Crunchy corn chips, spiced chicken, beans, corn, capsicum, cheese and a big fresh salad.
steps: Get ready
Heat oven to 200°C fan. Slice chicken breast into small bite-size pieces. Dice capsicum and tomatoes, shred lettuce, drain and rinse beans and corn.
Cook the chicken
Heat oil in a pan, add chicken, paprika and cumin. Sauté 7–9 minutes until golden and fully cooked to 75°C. Add capsicum for the last 3 minutes to soften slightly.
Build and bake

Spread corn chips over two lined baking trays. Scatter drained beans, corn, chicken and capsicum evenly; top with grated cheese. Bake 6–8 minutes until the cheese melts and everything is hot. Two trays avoid soggy chips.
Finish fresh
Scatter tomato, lettuce and diced avocado over each portion after baking. Offer plain Greek yoghurt on the side.
recipes.family: Reserve some chips, chicken and cheese without beans for any picky eaters.
recipes.kidJob: Scatter cheese over the chips and build their own toppings.
recipes.allergens: Milk; check corn chips and spice packaging for gluten or other allergens.
recipes.variation: Adjust the vegetable and carbohydrate portions to appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Use bagged shredded lettuce, canned beans and ready-made grated cheese.

nutrition.note: Chicken breast and beans provide substantial protein; chips and cheese portions vary.

recipes.title: Steak with Smoky Capsicum Sauce & Crispy Potatoes
recipes.shortTitle: Steak with Smoky Capsicum Sauce & Crispy Potatoes
recipes.subtitle: BBQ steak or chicken with smoky roasted-capsicum sauce, air-fryer potatoes and green vegetables.
steps: Air-fry the potatoes
Halve baby potatoes, toss in some oil and seasoning. Air-fry at 200°C for 18–22 minutes, shaking once, while preparing the meat and sauce.
Whiz the smoky sauce

Blend drained roasted capsicum with tomato paste, smoked paprika, balsamic and a little yoghurt in a blender or food processor until smooth. Taste, adjust seasoning and serve cool or gently warmed in a small saucepan. No garlic or cream needed.
BBQ steak and chicken separately

Season steak and grill to preferred doneness; rest for 5 minutes and slice against the grain. For Phoebe and Tobias, use flattened chicken breast portions, cooking them separately to at least 75°C in the centre. Avoid raw-meat cross-contact.
Finish the veg
Steam broccoli for 4–5 minutes until bright green. Serve steak or chicken with potatoes, plenty of broccoli, and smoky capsicum sauce on the side.
recipes.family: Phoebe and Tobias can have chicken with exactly the same vegetables and sauce.
recipes.kidJob: Wash potatoes and broccoli.
recipes.allergens: Milk in yoghurt; check jarred capsicum and tomato paste.
recipes.variation: Adjust the vegetable and carbohydrate portions to appetite.
recipes.prepTip: Jarred roasted capsicum makes the sauce quick; buy baby potatoes.

nutrition.note: Protein estimates vary with steak cut and whether individual plates use chicken.
